summary: A ten-case edge-origin block and a six-case public-contract block ran against both copies with loopback servers and the diagnostics channel. On the patched copy every edge case kept the base origin: a hostname base with a loopback-named path, the reverse, an uppercase-scheme absolute URL, an https-scheme absolute URL against an http base, a bare scheme prefix, query-only, empty, root and same-origin double-slash paths. On the vulnerable copy five cases changed origin, including the hostname/loopback mismatch in both directions, the uppercase absolute form, and the https absolute form, which attempted TLS to the foreign origin. The contract block was byte-identical between copies: numeric path and pathname produce the same InvalidArgumentError messages, a double-slash-only path produces the same TypeError, and relative, NUL-bearing and asterisk paths are accepted by both because resolution normalizes them before the request-level validator. Bracketed IPv6 binding failed with address-not-available, so IPv6 was recorded as a limitation at this step.
next_hint: Contract parity and unusual-origin containment hold; the remaining uncertainty is packaging. Export the unified diff, apply it to a freshly extracted pristine snapshot with a check-then-apply workflow, compare hashes with the working patched copy, parse the JSON-lines evaluator bundle exactly as an external consumer would, replay both harnesses on the bundle-patched tree, and add a one-site mutant negative control plus a recomputable manifest.
